functions.name: perfetto::base::FromPosixTimespec
functions.description: Converts a POSIX timespec (seconds + nanoseconds) to a std::chrono::nanoseconds duration (alias TimeNanos). Intended to adapt POSIX clock_gettime results to chrono-based durations.
requirements: ts.tv_nsec should be in the standard normalized range [0, 999,999,999] to represent a valid timespec (inferred from timespec semantics).

functions.name: perfetto::base::SleepMicroseconds
functions.description: Sleeps the calling thread for the specified interval in microseconds. Implementation is provided elsewhere; this is a declaration in the header.
requirements: interval_us is an unsigned count of microseconds; passing very large values may sleep for a long time (behavior depends on platform sleep granularity).
Callers should not assume high-precision or real-time guarantees; actual sleep may be longer than requested due to scheduler timing (general platform behavior).

functions.name: perfetto::base::InitializeTime
functions.description: Initializes timekeeping facilities used by this library. The exact behavior is not documented here; likely sets up platform-specific state for time queries. Details are unknown from this header.
requirements: Must be linked against the object/library providing its definition.
Ordering requirements or idempotency are unknown; if required to call before other time functions, that is not stated here.

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetWallTimeNs
functions.description: Returns a monotonic wall-clock-like time as a duration in nanoseconds since an unspecified epoch, suitable for measuring intervals. On most POSIX platforms uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC; on Apple uses mach_absolute_time; on Windows a platform-specific source. Not guaranteed to include time spent in system suspend.
requirements: No arguments; callable from any thread.
Monotonicity is expected; absolute reference epoch is unspecified and should not be persisted or mixed with real UTC time.

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetThreadCPUTimeNs
functions.description: Returns CPU time consumed by the calling thread as a duration in nanoseconds. On POSIX uses CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID or platform equivalents; on some platforms (e.g., WASM, NaCl) it returns 0.
requirements: No arguments; measures the calling thread only.
On platforms without support it returns 0; callers should handle a zero result as "unsupported or no CPU time consumed".

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetWallTimeRawNs
functions.description: Returns a raw monotonic time in nanoseconds, typically with minimal adjustments (e.g., CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW on Linux when available). Used for interval measurement where frequency/offset adjustments are undesirable. Falls back to regular monotonic time on platforms without a raw clock.
requirements: No arguments; callable from any thread.
Absolute epoch is unspecified; use only for relative timing.

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetBootTimeNs
functions.description: Returns time in nanoseconds since system boot. Where supported (e.g., Linux CLOCK_BOOTTIME), it includes time spent in system suspend. Falls back to monotonic time when a boot-time clock is not available or on platforms where it is not implemented.
requirements: No arguments; callable from any thread.
Absolute epoch is undefined; result is for relative measurements since boot and should not be treated as wall clock.

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetBootTimeS
functions.description: Returns time since boot as a std::chrono::seconds duration by casting GetBootTimeNs().
requirements: Relies on GetBootTimeNs(); all its requirements apply.

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetBootTimeMs
functions.description: Returns time since boot as a std::chrono::milliseconds duration by casting GetBootTimeNs().
requirements: Relies on GetBootTimeNs(); all its requirements apply.

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetWallTimeMs
functions.description: Returns monotonic wall time as a std::chrono::milliseconds duration by casting GetWallTimeNs().
requirements: Relies on GetWallTimeNs(); all its requirements apply.

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetWallTimeS
functions.description: Returns monotonic wall time as a std::chrono::seconds duration by casting GetWallTimeNs().
requirements: Relies on GetWallTimeNs(); all its requirements apply.

functions.name: perfetto::base::ToPosixTimespec
functions.description: Converts a std::chrono::milliseconds duration to a POSIX timespec with seconds and nanoseconds components.
requirements: Input is a duration; no special constraints.
The conversion truncates to whole seconds for tv_sec and computes the remainder in nanoseconds for tv_nsec.

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetTimeFmt
functions.description: Formats the current time according to the supplied format string and returns it as a std::string. The exact formatting rules are not specified here; likely follows strftime-style tokens. Details are unknown from this header.
requirements: fmt must be a valid format string for the underlying formatter; specifics are unknown in this header.
Callers should not assume thread-local static buffers; function returns a std::string.

functions.name: perfetto::base::TimeGm
functions.description: Converts a broken-down UTC time (struct tm) to a time_t-compatible timestamp (seconds since the Unix epoch). Wraps platform-specific timegm equivalents (_mkgmtime on Windows, timegm on POSIX). On NaCl it is unsupported and will fatally abort.
requirements: tms must be a valid, non-null pointer to a struct tm containing UTC fields.
Behavior on invalid or out-of-range fields depends on the platform timegm/_mkgmtime implementation.
Must not be used on NaCl builds (will fatal).

functions.name: perfetto::base::MkTime
functions.signature: int64_t perfetto::base::MkTime(int year, int month, int day, int h, int m, int s)
functions.description: Constructs a UTC timestamp (seconds since epoch) from human-friendly components: year (e.g., 2024), month (1–12), day (1–31), hour, minute, second. Internally builds a struct tm and calls TimeGm. Safer than timegm() regarding year and month interpretation.
requirements: year must be >= 1900 (checked via DCHECK).
month must be in the range 1..12 (checked via DCHECK).
day must be in the range 1..31 (checked via DCHECK).
h, m, s are passed through to struct tm without validation in this header; callers should provide sensible values to avoid undefined or implementation-defined behavior in TimeGm.
Requires TimeGm to be supported on the target platform (not NaCl).

functions.name: perfetto::base::Rdtsc
functions.description: Reads the CPU time-stamp counter (TSC) on x86_64 and returns its 64-bit value. Useful for very low-overhead cycle counting. Implemented via __rdtsc intrinsic on MSVC or inline assembly on GCC/Clang. Only available when PERFETTO_ARCH_CPU_X86_64 is enabled.
requirements: Must be built and executed on x86_64; the function is only defined under PERFETTO_ARCH_CPU_X86_64.
TSC frequency and behavior (e.g., invariance across power states/cores) are platform/CPU dependent; results are not wall-clock times and require calibration for conversion to time.
Serialization around rdtsc is not provided; if strict ordering is needed, callers should add fences (e.g., cpuid/rdtscp) externally.

functions.name: perfetto::base::GetTimezoneOffsetMins
functions.description: Returns the local timezone offset from UTC in minutes, if available; otherwise returns an empty optional. The header provides only the declaration; implementation details are elsewhere.
requirements: Callers must handle the empty optional case indicating the offset could not be determined on the current platform/context.

data_types.description: A string that specifies how to format date/time values. Typically follows strftime-style directives (e.g., %Y, %m, %d, %H, %M, %S) but may include arbitrary bytes. The formatter should interpret valid tokens and pass through or ignore invalid or unknown sequences. The string may include literal characters and percent-prefixed directives.

generators.generator:
import random
from typing import List

# This generator creates time format strings (strftime-like) with a mix of:
# - Common directives: %Y %m %d %H %M %S %f-like expansions via subsecond placeholders we encode as literals
# - Locale/weekday/month: %a %A %b %B %w %u %U %W
# - Timezone-related: %z %Z
# - Ordinals/Julian/day-of-year/ISO week/year: %j %V %G %g
# - Literal percent and edge cases: %% and stray % at end or followed by unknown chars
# - Width/flags: E/O modifiers, padding flags (_-0)
# - Separators, Unicode, and NUL bytes embedded (some formatters support embedded NUL handling via string length; C++ std::string can carry NULs)
# - Very long repeats to stress internal buffers but remain under 4096 bytes
# The output is bytes, used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the fuzzer.

COMMON_DIRECTIVES: List[str] = [
    "%Y", "%y", "%m", "%d", "%e", "%H", "%I", "%M", "%S",
    "%z", "%Z", "%p", "%P", "%f",  # %f often non-standard, leave for implementation-defined
    "%a", "%A", "%b", "%B", "%j", "%w", "%u", "%U", "%W",
    "%V", "%G", "%g", "%c", "%x", "%X", "%s",  # %s is GNU extension
    "%%"
]

# Optional modifiers and flags some implementations accept
MODIFIERS = ["%E", "%O"]
PADDING_FLAGS = ["_", "-", "0"]
WIDTHS = ["", "1", "2", "3", "4"]

# Potentially unknown/edge directives to test robustness
EDGE_DIRECTIVES = [
    "%Q", "%r", "%R", "%T", "%D", "%h", "%k", "%l", "%n", "%t",
    "%F", "%C"
]

LITERALS = [
    " ", "-", ":", "/", ".", ",", "T", "Z", "[", "]", "(", ")",
    "UTC", "GMT", "+", "-", "am", "pm"
]

UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "年", "月", "日", "時", "分", "秒",  # CJK
    "–", "—", "•", "·", "№",  # punctuation
    "mañana", "über", "résumé",  # Latin accents
]

# Some typical composite formats to exercise paths likely present in implementation
COMPOSITES = [
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
    "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S %z",
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z",
    "%Y-%j",  # day of year
    "%G-W%V-%u",  # ISO week date
    "%c", "%x", "%X",
]


def _rand(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]


def _maybe(r: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p


def _build_directive(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a directive with optional modifier and padding/width
    base = _rand(r, COMMON_DIRECTIVES + EDGE_DIRECTIVES)
    if base == "%%":
        return base
    # Some directives can accept flags; be permissive for coverage
    prefix = "%"
    if _maybe(r, 0.2):
        prefix = _rand(r, MODIFIERS)
    pad = _rand(r, PADDING_FLAGS) if _maybe(r, 0.3) else ""
    width = _rand(r, WIDTHS) if _maybe(r, 0.3) else ""
    # Construct like %_3d or %Od
    return prefix + pad + width + base[1:]


def _edge_cases(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cases = []
    # Lone percent at end
    cases.append("ending-%")
    # Percent followed by random char
    cases.append("%" + chr(r.randrange(32, 127)))
    # Mixed unknown sequences
    cases.append("%q %Q %_9K %" + chr(0x7F))
    # Empty string (some code paths may special-case)
    cases.append("")
    # Only literals
    cases.append("YYYYMMDDHHmmss")
    # NUL in middle
    cases.append("A\x00B%Y")
    return cases


def _assemble(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Start with a composite sometimes
    if _maybe(r, 0.6):
        parts.append(_rand(r, COMPOSITES))
    # Add a timezone-focused variant sometimes
    if _maybe(r, 0.5):
        parts.append("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z (%z)")
    # Add random sequence of directives and literals
    n = r.randint(3, 20)
    for _ in range(n):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.55:
            parts.append(_build_directive(r))
        elif choice < 0.75:
            parts.append(_rand(r, LITERALS))
        elif choice < 0.93:
            parts.append(_rand(r, UNICODE_SNIPPETS))
        else:
            parts.append(str(r.randint(0, 9999)).zfill(r.choice([2, 4])))
    # Occasionally prepend/append edge cases
    if _maybe(r, 0.3):
        parts.insert(0, _rand(r, _edge_cases(r)))
    if _maybe(r, 0.3):
        parts.append(_rand(r, _edge_cases(r)))
    # Occasionally repeat a segment to create longer inputs
    if _maybe(r, 0.4) and parts:
        seg = _rand(r, parts)
        parts.append(seg * r.randint(2, 6))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Ensure not exceeding 4096 bytes when encoded utf-8
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
        try:
            s = b.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        except Exception:
            pass
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose between a curated edge-case, a composite, or a random assembly
    mode = r.random()
    if mode < 0.2:
        fmt = _rand(r, _edge_cases(r))
    elif mode < 0.35:
        # Build with heavy timezone/ISO variants
        iso = _rand(r, [
            "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z",
            "%G-W%V-%u %H:%M:%S %z",
            "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S %Z",
            "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z (%z)",
        ])
        # Add trailing literals or escaped percent
        tail = r.choice(["", " ", " %%", " Z", " UTC", " "+_rand(r, UNICODE_SNIPPETS)])
        fmt = iso + tail
    else:
        fmt = _assemble(r)
    data = fmt.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Guarantee non-empty to exercise code paths
    if not data:
        data = b"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
    # Cap size
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
